recognize_zh: 大量原始細胞背景中，可見多個巨核細胞核呈分離的圓形小核（separated/disjointed nuclei）或單葉圓核，體積偏小；芽細胞增加合併這種巨核細胞發育異常，應聯想 AML with inv(3)/t(3;3)。
features: Numerous medium to large blasts with fine chromatin, nucleoli and scant basophilic cytoplasm
Several megakaryocytes with multiple separate round nuclear lobes (disjointed/widely separated nuclei)
Megakaryocytes with single round non-lobated nuclei and moderate pale granular cytoplasm
Megakaryocytes are relatively small compared with normal mature forms
Scattered small lymphocytes and occasional maturing granulocytes
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear is hypercellular with a predominance of medium to large blasts showing fine chromatin, nucleoli and scant basophilic cytoplasm. Multiple megakaryocytes are dysplastic, with widely separated round nuclear lobes or single non-lobated round nuclei in relatively small cells. Residual maturing granulocytes are sparse. Findings are consistent with acute myeloid leukemia with prominent megakaryocytic dysplasia, a pattern suggestive of AML with inv(3)(q21.3q26.2)/t(3;3) (GATA2::MECOM); confirmation requires cytogenetics or MECOM FISH.

ddx.vs: Multilineage dysplasia is shared, so the distinction rests on demonstrating a 3q26 MECOM rearrangement by karyotype or FISH.
MDS-EB has a similar megakaryocytic dysplasia but fewer blasts (<20% in WHO 2016) than the blast-predominant field seen here.
In AMKL the blasts themselves are megakaryoblasts (CD41/CD61+ with blebs) rather than non-megakaryocytic blasts accompanied by dysplastic mature megakaryocytes.
